solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lightly pad neckwear wrapped round shirt, say, back to front

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: a tie is worn round the neck

indicators.note: the last letter of the garment word is brought round to the front

parts.note: a shirt is an example of a top, a garment for the upper body

explanation.surface: Someone's neckwear is knotted round a shirt that has been put on backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk on the balls of the feet is to pad about lightly and quietly.

clue.text: Act to cover renegade

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act on stage
to coat is to cover with a layer

explanation.surface: A theatre act provides cover for someone who has defected.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts their side for the other, the classic sense of a traitor who switches allegiance.

clue.text: Some links hanging from short rod — one was entirely yellow

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece hangs below the other, so it comes second
the rod word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a pole is a long rod
Troon is a Scottish seaside golf course, one of the Open venues; a links is a coastal golf course

explanation.surface: Chain links dangle from a shortened rod, and something was coloured all yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging from' puts TROON beneath POL (POLE cut short by 'short'). Yellow means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: A coward is called yellow, and this old word names an utter coward.

clue.text: Prig quitting monstrously, in a repulsive way

indicators.note: the letters of the first word leave the longer adverb, scattered but in order

parts.note: prodigiously means enormously, monstrously in size

explanation.surface: A prig leaves while behaving monstrously, in a repellent manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quitting' removes P, R, I and G, in that order, from PRODIGIOUSLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means hateful or repellent, so acting repulsively is acting this way.

clue.text: One blows out air using silver tube with brown coating

indicators.note: the brown abbreviation lies on either side like a coat round the rest

parts.note: BR is a standard abbreviation for brown
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a pipe is a tube

explanation.surface: A silver tube with a brown finish is used by someone blowing out air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coating' puts AGPIPE inside BR. 'Air' is a tune, not breath.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish piper plays a tune, or air, by blowing into the bag of the instrument.

clue.text: Caught abandoning corrupt acclamation of a body

indicators.note: corrupt suggests something debased and altered, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the caught letter leaves the word acclamation

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone caught out abandons a rigged show of public approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' drops one C from ACCLAMATION; 'corrupt' then rearranges the remaining ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy is the study of a body's structure, so the adjective describes things relating to a body.

clue.text: Don appearing in drag, performing now?

parts.note: to drag is to pull
a show that is on is being performed at the moment

explanation.surface: A university don turns up in drag, perhaps in a show running right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a university teacher but is the verb meaning to put clothing on.
explanation.definitionFit: To don a garment is to put it on, as one does with a jumper.

clue.text: Canned chop suey, void of nuts

indicators.note: canned is slang for drunk, so the letters reel about into a new order
void means emptied, so only the outer letters of the word stay

explanation.surface: A tin of chop suey turns out to have no nuts in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'void' empties SUEY to SY; 'Canned' rearranges CHOP plus SY.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, someone called a psycho is crazy, just as nuts means mad.

clue.text: Unit in northern area runs to secure help from the south

indicators.note: in a down answer, reading from the bottom upwards turns the letters round
the letters for northern, area and runs hold the help word fast within them

parts.note: R stands for runs on a cricket scorecard
aid means help

explanation.surface: A military unit in a northern region runs to get help from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' puts AID inside NAR, giving NAIDAR; 'from the south' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the standard SI measure of angle, the arc equal in length to the circle's radius.

clue.text: Again put down person who calls round heartlessly

indicators.note: the word is turned round and read backwards
the central letter of the caller word is taken away

parts.note: a dialler is someone making a phone call

explanation.surface: Someone pays a cold, unfeeling visit and puts somebody down once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' takes the middle L from DIALLER; 'round' turns DIALER backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laid a second time, such as a carpet or track, has been put down again.

clue.text: Passage joined on both sides with motley irises

indicators.note: the joined word sits on either side of the passage word

parts.note: to wed is to join in marriage
an alley is a narrow passage

explanation.surface: A passageway joined at each end has irises of mixed colours.
explanation.definitionFit: One older sense describes eyes with pale or discoloured irises, streaked or uneven in colour.

clue.text: Hollow church suppressing 'Irish Question'

indicators.note: the church letters sit on top of and hold down the other letters

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: The church stifles discussion of the historic Irish Question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressing' puts IRQU inside CE. The Irish Question was the nineteenth-century debate over Irish home rule.
explanation.definitionFit: This geology term names a bowl-shaped hollow scooped out by a glacier at a mountain's head.

clue.text: Woman departs over corruption by most of police

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over
rot is decay or corruption

indicators.note: the police word loses its last letter

parts.note: the heat is slang for the police

explanation.surface: A woman leaves after the police uncover widespread corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims HEAT to HEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothea is a female given name, such as the heroine of Middlemarch.

clue.text: One reason for rash South American to break into Beetle left by British

indicators.note: the South American word breaks into the beetle word
the British letter departs from the beetle word

parts.note: a scarab is a beetle sacred in ancient Egypt
a Latin is a Latin American person

explanation.surface: A South American breaks into a Volkswagen Beetle left behind by a Briton, a hasty act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One reason for rash' reads as a hasty motive, but rash is the skin eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet fever, another name for this illness, produces a red skin rash.

clue.text: With red vision, optical rimless specs will need to be adjusted

indicators.note: adjusted means altered, so the gathered letters are reordered
without its rim, only the inner letters of the word stay

explanation.surface: Rimless glasses need adjusting to correct someone's vision, perhaps to cut out redness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rimless' cuts SPECS to PEC; 'will need to be adjusted' rearranges OPTICAL plus PEC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone furious enough to be seeing red is livid with rage, as if close to a seizure.

clue.text: Bull-headed type of youngster penning letter overseas

indicators.note: the youngster word encloses the letter, as in a pen

parts.note: a minor is someone under age
tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so foreign

explanation.surface: A stubborn sort of youngster writes a letter abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bull-headed' means stubborn on the surface but literally has a bull's head here.
explanation.definitionFit: The monster of Cretan myth had a man's body and a bull's head.

clue.text: In America, notice socialist's insolence?

parts.note: pink means mildly left-wing, socialist; the 's adds S
lip is cheek, insolence

explanation.surface: An American takes notice of a left-winger's cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notice' is a dismissal notice, not attention.
explanation.definitionFit: An American employee is given a slip of this colour as formal notice of dismissal.

clue.text: Start to accept the setter's making a comeback and hit agreement

indicators.note: the start word takes in the other pieces

parts.note: to shy is to start back suddenly, as a startled horse does

indicators.note: the setter's word comes back, reading the other way

parts.note: my is how the setter refers to something of their own
a pat is a light hit

explanation.surface: To begin accepting the setter's return to form, everyone hits on agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' is the verb: a horse that shies starts back in alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in sympathy with a view means being in accord with it.

clue.text: Line out of Albert's theory at first caught imagination

indicators.note: the caught letter goes at the start

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the line letter goes out of the theory

parts.note: Albert Einstein's best-known theory is relativity

explanation.surface: A line drops out of Einstein's theory and at first catches the imagination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes L from RELATIVITY; 'at first' puts C before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Inventiveness and imagination are both the capacity to come up with original ideas.

clue.text: Still very happy, although missing The City

indicators.note: the City letters are missing from the happy word

parts.note: ecstatic means overjoyed
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone is still delighted, despite having left the City behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcode begins EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unmoving or stationary is still.

clue.text: Cast almost put round funny bone

indicators.note: the shortened word is turned round, reading backwards
the last letter of the first word is left off

parts.note: rum means odd or funny

explanation.surface: A plaster cast is nearly put round someone's funny bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny bone' looks like one phrase but splits: funny is wordplay, bone the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This triangular bone sits at the base of the spine, between the hip bones.

clue.text: View some expat in autobiographical film

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, running across them

explanation.surface: An exile is invited to watch a film about their own life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie but means a thin surface layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheen or thin coating that forms on old bronze or wood is a surface film.

clue.text: Tough head removed from type of seed on hollow tree

indicators.note: the seed piece is placed on, after, the tree piece
with its inside hollowed out, only the outside letters of the word stay
the seed word loses its first letter

parts.note: caraway is a seed used as a spice

explanation.surface: A hard-headed seed is removed from a particular type grown on a hollow tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' leaves TE from TREE; 'head removed from' takes C from CARAWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough here is a noun, a reckless young hooligan or rowdy.

clue.text: Arouse dispute about UKIP when one's off out

indicators.note: the dispute word is turned about, reading backwards

parts.note: a row is a dispute

indicators.note: out signals the remaining letters are put out of order
the one letter goes off, leaving the party name

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A row erupts about the UK Independence Party when one member walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ROW into WOR; 'off' takes I from UKIP and 'out' rearranges UKP into KUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir someone into agitation or excitement is to arouse them.

clue.text: Great outburst about keeping sin in check to start with

indicators.note: the reversed outburst keeps the sin word inside it
the outburst word turns about, reading backwards

parts.note: a fit is a sudden outburst
to err is to sin

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two following words are taken

explanation.surface: An angry outburst helps keep sin in check from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, superb or excellent things are called great.

clue.text: Everyone trapped by rainy weather ready to come out of it?

definitions.text: ready to come out of it?

indicators.note: the everyone word is held inside the weather word

parts.note: the wet means rainy weather
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone stuck in a downpour wants to get out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is cash (readies), which comes out of the pouch where it is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready money is kept in a pocket purse, so cash comes out of it when paying.

clue.text: Yours truly absent after firm gives leave

indicators.note: the setter's pieces come after the firm

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
yours truly is a jocular way of saying me
away means absent

explanation.surface: With the setter away, the company grants a period of leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart from a place is to leave it, the intransitive verb.

clue.text: Equipped to remove signal saying: Stop — unknown stump up ahead

indicators.note: the signal word is taken away from the end of the first word

parts.note: prepared means equipped or ready
a red traffic light signals stop
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Something is fitted to remove a stop sign, with an unknown party paying in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to remove' takes RED from PREPARED, leaving PREPA.
explanation.definitionFit: To stump up is to pay, so paying in advance is paying ahead of time.
